name: Ui_PanelState_Enter0EOr10
summary: Cancels any running panel action and enters panel state 0x0E with the +0xB8/+0xBC duration when the pending card id f_234 is 0, otherwise state 0x10 with the +0x48/+0x4C duration; both branches rebind the slot control, and the 0x0E branch clears f_234 to -1.
evidence: Named caller maybe_Ui_Panel_UpdateStateC reaches it in the >= 0x33 branch. Its closest sibling, maybe_Ui_PanelState_Enter11Or0E (0x001E21D8), has the identical two-branch shape: the same 0x001E3BEC state setter, the same f_234 test, the same 0x0072A944 f_48/f_4C and f_B8/f_BC duration pairs, the same f_234 = -1 clear and the same Ui_Slot_BindControl rebind - it just selects state 0x11/0x0E, while this function selects 0x10/0x0E. Ui_PanelState_Enter16/Enter0B call the same setter. So the state-machine role and the two states are proven.

name: Battle_Ui_BuildMemberActionEntries
signature: void Battle_Ui_BuildMemberActionEntries(BattleUiContext* self, BattleActor* actor, u32 actionId, u32 flags)
summary: Fills the next free entry of the battle HUD's 48-entry (0x90-byte) action table for up to six action slots of an actor: checks the actor against the slot's type byte, copies the 0x58-byte action descriptor, stores the actor pointer and validity byte and spawns the type-0xF balloon when the battle is in 3D mode.
evidence: The table walk (48 entries at +0x4AF, six 0x18-byte slots per entry), the descriptor copy and the actor/validity stores are all visible. The callees are now named (Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor type 0xF, maybe_Battle_FindTargetIndexByState, Game_GetDataManager/Data_LookupSubRecord) and the neighbours are Battle_Ui_SpawnPopupForUnit / Battle_Ui_RefreshAllMemberRows, which pins the battle member-row logic; only the display meaning of the 0x58 block is inferred.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_SpawnBalloonTypeC
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_SpawnBalloonTypeC(BattleBalloonUi* ui, u32 count, PartyMember* member, int skipFlag, u32 delay, u32 flag)
summary: Resets the member's displayed value, appends a type-5 bookkeeping record for (member, count) to the balloon list at ui+0xBC, plays SE 0x1E and, unless skipFlag is set, shows the type-0xC balloon at the member's anchor. The old 'Cancel' label was an unverified reading of balloon type 0xC.
evidence: The body is fully readable and contains no cancellation logic: member vtable +0x40 reset, Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnBalloonEntry with record type 5, Sound_PlaySeById(0x1E), then Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor(type 0xC). Its named sibling Ui_Balloon_SpawnForMember uses type 6 the same way, so the numeric balloon type is the only provable fact; 'Cancel' was invented.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_SpawnBalloonTypeCForSlot
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_SpawnBalloonTypeCForSlot(BattleBalloonUi* self, u32 count, u32 slot, int skipFlag, u32 delay, u32 flag)
summary: Slot-indexed twin of 0x001F6CAC: resolves the member through vtable +0x48(self, slot), resets its displayed value, queues the type-5 record, plays SE 0x1E only when the member's f_10 flag is set, and spawns the same type-0xC balloon at its anchor.
evidence: Byte-for-byte the same named calls as 0x001F6CAC (Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnBalloonEntry, Sound_PlaySeById 0x1E, Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor type 0xC) with the member obtained through the slot accessor; the only differences are the slot lookup and the f_10 gate on the sound. 'Cancel' is no better supported here than in the ARM twin, so the name states the balloon type instead.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_ActionEntryTail
summary: Not an independent function: 0x003C4A20 is a cold tail block (no prologue, live r4-r8) that increments member+0xDF0 when the battle work's 3D flag (+0x4244) is set, then pops. Ghidra's 'BuildMemberActionEntriesB' body is a recycled decompilation of 0x003C3F5C's internal labels and must not be merged as a separate routine.
evidence: Disassembly at 0x003C4A20 starts with bl Os_GetGameWork and never pushes a frame; it pops at 0x003C4A54. The decompiled LAB_003c40f8/LAB_003c4180 labels belong to 0x003C3F5C, which proves the readable body is not this address's own code. The only real operation visible is the conditional increment of member+0xDF0 under the 3D-mode flag.

name: Battle_Ui_SpawnSoundBalloon
signature: void Battle_Ui_SpawnSoundBalloon(BattleBalloonUi* ui, int count, PartyMember* member, u32 delay, u32 flag)
summary: Plays SE 0x12B and, unless the UI busy flag is set, resets the member's displayed value with the count; when delay is zero it then shows the type-9 balloon at the member's anchor.
evidence: Both callees are named (Sound_PlaySeById, Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor) and the ids are literal (SE 0x12B, balloon type 9); the member vtable +0x40 reset is the same one used by the sibling balloon spawners in this family. The decompiler swapped the member/count operands, but the type-9 balloon plus dedicated SE is exactly a 'sound balloon'.

name: Gfx_EffectParams_InitSet
summary: Creates the nineteen fixed effect parameters of the status/equipment page on the owner at +0x4D78 (types 0xC/0x10/0x22/0x23/0x2A/8/0/0x18/7/2/0x17/0x16/0xD/0x11, some only in 2D or 3D mode) and then links one extra 0x1BC-byte parameter block built from the shared template.
evidence: The sole caller is the named Menu_Status_InitEffectParams and every call goes through the named Gfx_EffectParams_Create (0x003D13C4); the tail allocates the same 0x1BC-byte block and links it with Gfx_EffectParams_LoadTemplate. The decompilation is not damaged in substance - the unaff_r4..r6 are Ghidra's invented trailing arguments after the 8-byte-alignment prologue (a documented trap in FACTS), and the 19 creates plus the template link are fully readable; only the meaning of each type id is unknown.

name: Menu_InitPageEffects
summary: Page setup for a menu page: picks the page id (f_442C, or f_489C in 2D mode), requests the page's BGM category and creates the page's effect parameters - 8/5 normally, or 8/10 + 0/0x3C + 7/0 + 2/0 for page 2, which also raises f_423E.
evidence: The body is a page switch over the named Gfx_EffectParams_Create plus the named maybe_Sound_ApplyCategoryBgmState, and its page-id sources f_442C/f_489C are the same fields used by the named Menu_Status_InitEffectParams. No text or input handler is registered, so the page-effect initialiser reading holds.

name: maybe_Menu_InitBaseEffectParams
summary: Creates the five shared effect parameters (0x13/0x15/0x14/9/10) on the menu effect owner after resetting the cursor id f_4211 to 0xFF, flushes them through 0x003D1144 and requests the category BGM from f_4200.
evidence: These are exactly the first five Gfx_EffectParams_Create ids (and the f_4211 = 0xFF reset) of the named Menu_Status_InitEffectParams, which afterwards calls Menu_InitCursorEffectParams and page-specific sets; so this is the shared/base parameter set, not a second full page. The old 'Alt' suffix only said 'another copy'.

name: Menu_MeasureAverageActorWidth
summary: Measures four actor-group records at self+0x4298: for each one it walks the actor list summing the two u16 sizes at +0x3E/+0x42 of every live node, counts the group's widget children (Ui_Widget_CountChildren at self+0x428C) and returns the average width (sum of sizes / total children, or the raw sum when the count is < 1) in s0.
evidence: Disassembly shows the real body: a four-iteration loop (r7 = 0..3) over 0x1C-stride records at self+0x4298, the inner linked-list walk accumulating f_3E + f_42 via vcvt/vadd into s17, and bl 0x5797D8 (Ui_Widget_CountChildren) accumulating s16; it ends with vdiv s18 = s17/s16 and vmov s0, s18 at 0x0020C0B8. The damaged-looking coprocessor_function/in_cr markers are Ghidra's VFP decode artefacts, and the cited disassembly shows there are no Gfx_EffectParams_Create calls in the actual code - the decompiled create tail is Ghidra spilling into the following function.

name: maybe_Menu_MeasureAverageActorWidthTail
summary: False function entry: 0x0020C08C is inside Menu_MeasureAverageActorWidth (0x0020BFF0), not a function start. The 'thirty Gfx_EffectParams_Create calls' in the readable C are Ghidra decoding the middle of the measure loop; do not merge this address as an independent routine.
evidence: Disassembly has no prologue at 0x0020C08C (live r7/s16 registers) and the loop branch at 0x0020C0A4 jumps back to 0x0020C00C, which is inside 0x0020BFF0; the enclosing function pops at 0x0020C0C0. The calls attributed to this entry (Ui_Widget_CountChildren and 0x0020BFF0) are real instructions of that measure loop.

name: maybe_Menu_WriteEffectStateByte
signature: void maybe_Menu_WriteEffectStateByte(MenuState* self, u8 value, int offset)
summary: Stores one byte at self+offset and then appends the standard four-entry menu effect-parameter block (8/10, 0/0x6F, 7/0, 2/0) to the menu's effect owner at self+0x4D78.
evidence: The write is `*(u8*)(count + list) = value` with list then advanced by 0x4D78 - the same menu effect-owner offset used by the named Menu_Status_InitEffectParams and Menu_InitCursorEffectParams - and the four follow-up ids are their fixed command block. The old 'Gfx_DisplayList' prefix named a subsystem the body never touches.

name: Ui_Overlay_RefreshActorAttachments
summary: Clears the overlay's animation flag f_284 and then refreshes the attach transform of every visible field actor whose type word f_30 carries the 0x20000040 attach bits, by walking the field actor list (work+8 -> +0x54) and calling maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateAttachTransform.
evidence: All nine callers are overlay/actor state-change paths (Ui_OverlaySlot_ApplyStateChange, Ui_Overlay_RefreshSlots, Field_Object2D_RunStateSequence, Event_Rura_End, ...), and both call sites run it immediately after changing the overlay mode self->f_281. The in-loop callee is the attach-transform updater (Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection + weapon animation time), so 'ResetElementAnimation' described only the f_284 clear and missed the actual work.

name: Party_MoveEquipmentToMemberOrBag
signature: void Party_MoveEquipmentToMemberOrBag(u32 unused, int srcMemberId, int srcSlot, u32 itemId, int dstMemberId)
summary: Equips itemId into slot srcSlot of the source member after unequipping whatever was there, and routes the unequipped item to the destination member, or to the bag when dstMemberId is 0xFF; it then re-adds/equips the requested item and refreshes the bag.
evidence: FACTS' equipment ranges (0xA4..0x9BF, 0xB19..0xB1C) and the member record func_0035EB98 are visible, together with the named Member_RemoveItemAtSlot / Party_Member_EquipInventorySlot / Party_Member_UnequipSlotAndRefresh. The 0xFF branch calls func_00612008(work+0x24ACC, item, 1) - the ItemBag add - while the other branch resolves a second member and calls func_00191DA4; so it moves equipment to a member or to the bag, not only 'between members'.

name: Shop_BuyItemForMember
signature: int Shop_BuyItemForMember(u32* screen, int itemId, int count, u32 memberIndex, int equipSlot)
summary: Buys count units of an item: multiplies the record price (+0x18) by count, subtracts it from the party gold through the ItemBag (work+0x24A98), then gives the item to a party member (index < 0x1F), equipping it in the requested slot when asked, or adds the remaining units to the bag.
evidence: The price/gold arithmetic is explicit (record f_18 * count, func_00613FC0(work+0x24A98, -total)), the member branch uses func_0035EB98 + maybe_Member_SetItemAtSlot / Party_Member_EquipInventorySlot, and the leftover units go through func_00612008(work+0x24ACC). The named caller maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_SelectEntryEx uses the return value as the number of items gained, which matches the purchase role.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_CtorTail
summary: False function entry: 0x00310900 is inside the constructor at 0x00310844 (no prologue, live r4-r8, falls through). The recovered 'Text_LineFillCharsEx' body is a misdecode; the enclosing constructor stores vtable 0x00762F54 and initialises a UI state object with a type byte (default 0x45), pointers at +0x8/+0xC/+0x10 and parameters at +0x18/+0x1C.
evidence: Disassembly: 0x00310844 starts with push {r4..fp,lr} and runs through 0x00310900, which begins mid-sequence with bl 0x63DF14 and no frame; the next real prologue is only at 0x00310C90. The words at 0x00310C64/0x00310C68 resolve to vtable 0x00762F54 and globals. The item/inventory-looking recovered calls are therefore artefacts of decompiling from a mid-function address, and 'Text_LineFillCharsEx' cannot stand either way.

name: Battle_Unit_RefreshDisplayValuesB
summary: Second display-refresh variant of a battle unit: resolves the unit's party-member record, checks the enemy display slot and marks the layout dirty when it changed, converts the member's +0x746/+0xEC6/+0xB06 values to floats for the message rows and returns the (f_746, f_EC6) pair.
evidence: It is the exact body of the refined Battle_Unit_RefreshDisplayValues (0x00496650) with the adjacent field triplet (+0x746/+0xEC6/+0xB06 instead of +0x740/+0xEC0/+0xB00); it is called from Battle_Monster_GetHpBarRatio's special-unit branch, exactly where 0x004972EC is called from GetMpBarRatio. No defence value is returned, so the old 'GetMagicDefence' label was wrong.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_AddUnitToRowGroup
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_AddUnitToRowGroup(void* unused, BattleUnit* unit, u32 groupId, UiTargetRow* rows)
summary: Adds a battle unit to one of ten 0x24-byte target-row groups: finds the row keyed by +0x784 (or claims the first 0xFFFF row), stores the unit in the first free of four slots (+0x774..+0x780), adds the unit's HP and MP bar ratios into +0x78C/+0x790 and copies its +0x10 flag into the row's busy byte.
evidence: The two float callees are the named Battle_Monster_GetHpBarRatio/Battle_Monster_GetMpBarRatio (0x00492520/0x004900A8), and their results are summed into the row fields; the named caller Battle_ActionCommand_ProcessSkillEffect passes affected battle units. The old 'Ui_TextLayout_AddToRowGroup' treated those units as glyphs - there is no glyph metric call in the body.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_AddUnitToRowGroupWithValue
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_AddUnitToRowGroupWithValue(UiTargetRow* rows, BattleUnit* unit, u32 groupId, u16 value)
summary: Twin of 0x00279760 with a second pass over the ten target rows: after inserting the unit into a matching or free row and adding its HP/MP ratios, it also stores a caller-supplied u16 in the row's +0x788 payload field and mirrors the unit's flag into +0x794.
evidence: Disassembly is a byte-for-byte copy of 0x00279760 except for the extra strh to +0x788, and it calls the same named HP/MP ratio getters, so it aggregates battle units rather than glyphs. The only plausible caller signal is the battle skill-effect path; the equipment-function caller association in the old dossier is a symbol-range artefact (no bl to this address exists in 0x0027A118).

name: Actor2D_SpriteNode_DtorB
summary: Destructor of the 2D actor sprite node built by Actor2D_SpriteNode_CtorB: restores the class's two vtable halves (g_actor2DSpriteNodeClassDescB + 0x9C), destroys its eight 0x48-byte sprite entries, installs the base 0x0075D55C vtables, unlinks the embedded scene node, runs Field_Object_DtorBase and frees the block.
evidence: The immediately preceding function 0x002B41F8 is the named Actor2D_SpriteNode_CtorB, which allocates exactly 8 x 0x48 bytes at +0xa6 with the same g_actor2DSpriteNodeClassDescB vtable; this body destroys that same array via std_destroy_range(self+0xa6, 8) and then falls into the base destructor. It is the ...B-class twin of the refined maybe_Actor2D_SpriteNode_DtorC (0x0029081C), whose body is identical for g_actor2DSpriteNodeClassDesc. 'Field2D_Actor' guessed the wrong class family.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite_CreateChild_75AE04
summary: Child-object factory of the sprite class whose destructor sits at 0x003A32C8: forwards the resource name to Gfx_SceneNode_LoadMeshByName, allocates a 0xAC-byte child (vtable 0x0075AE04), stores the owner at +0x20 and constructs two 0x40-byte sequence entries (ctor 0x006CBF70).
evidence: It directly follows the named Gfx_Sprite_DeletingDtorC (0x003A32C8) and precedes Gfx_ModelPart_InitSimple; disassembly is the standard allocate-child/copy-defaults template. The actual child vtable literal is 0x0075AE04 and no model-part list is initialised, so 'ModelPartList_Init' was wrong on both class and role; the family is inferred from the adjacent sprite destructor, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_CreateChild_75AEB8
summary: Creates a 0xEC-byte child from the caller's resource name: Gfx_SceneNode_LoadMeshByName attaches the mesh, then the child is allocated with vtable 0x0075AEB8, owner at +0x20, and three 0x40-byte sequence entries (ctor 0x006CCF5C). Its callers are field-gimmick update paths.
evidence: The readable tail shows the child vtable is actually 0x0075AEB8 (not the 0x0076A158/0x0076D2F8 set the old doc claimed), and the callers are the field-gimmick update functions 0x005D9334/0x005D94B8/0x005DDF48/0x005E15D0. The UI sub-widget reading was therefore wrong; the exact field class is still open, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_CreateChild
summary: Factory of the 2D sprite class whose destructor is at 0x002F41F0: loads the caller's resource as the node mesh, allocates a 0xAC-byte child (vtable 0x0075AB7C), stores the owner and constructs two 0x40-byte sequence entries (ctor 0x006C8624).
evidence: It immediately follows the named Gfx_Sprite2D_DeletingDtorC (0x002F41F0), and the literal pool at 0x002F4368 resolves to child vtable 0x0075AB7C, ctor 0x006C8624 and default table 0x00725E4C; the body is the same factory template as the sibling classes. 'SceneNode_InitChildB' guessed the wrong family and 'Init' the wrong role.

name: maybe_Gfx_CreateChildObject_75B260
summary: Lazily creates the 0x12C-byte child object of a model/scene class (vtable 0x0075B260), stores the owner at +0x20 and constructs 0x20 eight-byte entries with ctor 0x006D2344; on failure it falls back to copying the 32-word default block at 0x0072D818. No GPU register access is present.
evidence: The body only allocates, constructs and copies defaults - there is no PICA register window (0x0200..) or command write anywhere, so 'SharedRenderState_Apply' described a call shape that is not in the code. The neighbours are model/container helpers (Model_ApplyPartVisibility, Ui_CharaStatus_HideModelA).

name: Field_Action_Step_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the field footstep action: runs the walk-task base constructor, installs the walk-task vtable, loads the motion-name pairs for records 1 and 4, then installs g_fieldActionStepVtable and initialises the step state (+0x74..+0x80) with the -1 sentinel at +0x80.
evidence: It installs g_fieldActionStepVtable and is followed immediately by Field_Action_Step_DeletingDtor and Field_Action_StepBehaviour_DeletingDtor (0x00301A94/0x00301AA4); its named callers Actor_Action_SkullRunCtor and Monster_UpdateBehavior use it as their base action constructor. 'Actor_Action_TwoStepCtor' named the mechanism and the wrong subsystem.

name: SaveData_RebuildPartyRoster
summary: Rebuilds all 31 party-member records from the character master records (func_0063F8F0 + Party_Member_InitFromMasterRecord) and, for member 0, walks its 24 inventory item ids, resolving each item and marking the item and its variants in the save ownership bitmask at partyWork+0x24A98+0x4B30.
evidence: It is the same logic as the confident Party_Member_SyncOwnedItemsToBitmask (0x0035F38C), looped over every member index, and its named caller SaveData_ResetMemberTriggers calls it right after resetting the text pages and the party container. There is no text-page or glyph work in the body, so 'Ui_Window_RebuildSlotPages' was wrong.

name: Field_Actor_UpdateEquipDisplay
summary: Refreshes a field actor's visible equipment: sets the dirty flag +0x271, classifies the member's two equipped ids, and for the dual-display styles 9/10 writes the item-name block to the +0x700 text handle and attaches the matching weapon/armour model slice through Model_AttachSlot_Setup using the member's costume flag.
evidence: The body is explicit: func_006292F0(member, 0/1) equipped ids -> Item_ClassifyDualEquipCategory -> Item_LookupRecord -> func_004EDA68(self+0x700, ...) plus Model_AttachSlot_Setup(model->f_160, ..., PartyMember_GetCharRecordFlag430). Its sibling 0x00377420 performs the same text-only update, confirming the display-refresh role.

name: Battle_CompareEquipPairStyle
signature: int Battle_CompareEquipPairStyle(BattleActor* actor, int arg2, int mode, u32 itemId)
summary: Compares the equipped-pair display style of a battle actor with the style of a supplied item (mode 0) or another item pair (mode 1): resolves the actor's member record and its two equipped item ids, classifies both with Item_ClassifyDualEquipCategory and returns non-zero when the styles differ.
evidence: The battle unit is fetched from battle work +0x4254 by the actor's f_768 id, the two equipped ids come from func_006292F0 and are resolved through the named Item_LookupRecord / Item_ClassifyDualEquipCategory, and both modes end in a style-equality return. No caller proves a different role, so the old name stands but confidence stays moderate.

name: Field_Actor_SetEquippedPairText
summary: Rebuilds the actor's equipped-item label: for the dual-display styles 9/10 it resolves the member's equipped item ids and writes one or two item-name strings into the text handle at +0x700 (style 9 = one line, style 10 = two lines).
evidence: The equipped ids come from func_006292F0(member, 0/1), the display style from Item_ClassifyDualEquipCategory, and the sink is func_004EDA68(self+0x700, ...). It only reads item rows to format display names - the item-lookup flag does not apply because there is no item or inventory mutation here.

name: Ui_RecordDetailWindow_HandleTabInput
summary: Applies the record-detail window's tab/sub-page selection: on cancel it pops the sub-pane; on confirm it switches on the current page kind, selects the matching text column (+0x47/+0x61/+0x7B) and pushes the matching page for kinds 0..2, while kinds 3..6 call the slot virtuals +0x2C..+0x38 and play sounds 0x2C..0x2F.
evidence: All callees are now named record-detail/widget helpers (Ui_RecordDetailWindow_UpdateText, Ui_TextWidget_SetTextIndex, Ui_WidgetStack_PushAt, Ui_Window_PopSubPane, Ui_MonsterBook_FillEntry), and the switch over the page kind at self[0x21]+0xC with the three column offsets is fully readable; 'HandleTabInput' is an honest description of that confirm/cancel dispatch.

name: maybe_Ui_RecordDetailWindow_BuildRowsTail
summary: False function entry: 0x0037C8E0 is inside Ui_RecordDetailWindow_BuildRows (0x0037C6F8), which pushes at 0x0037C6F8 and pops at 0x0037C978. This fragment counts owned item types, formats a wide string and sets an inverse flag as part of the row build; the recovered 'RefreshPage' body with virtual +0x24/+0x28 calls is not present in the disassembly.
evidence: Disassembly at 0x0037C8E0 has no prologue or epilogue of its own (the enclosing function's pop is at 0x0037C978), and the real calls are 0x629E40 (Item_CountOwnedTypesFromBitmask), 0x6F0F1C (wide-string format) and 0x3B3334, matching the record-row text build rather than a page refresh.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_BuildRowsByItemKind
summary: Clears the row count and walks item ids 0..0x24D through func_0063E998/Item_LookupRecord, keeping the ids whose record kind byte (+0x0C) equals the requested category and appending them (with the 0x8000 bit from Ui_ListWindow_MatchesFlagFilter) to the row table.
evidence: The filter is record->f_C == category - FACTS documents +0x0C as the item kind - and every iteration resolves the id from the 0x24E-entry table through the named Item_LookupRecord. Nothing reads character or kana text, so 'ByCharCategory' was wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_BuildRowsForEquippableItems
summary: Walks item ids 0..0x24D and appends those accepted by any of the three equipment predicates func_0066CCEC/func_0066C978/func_0066C950, with the 0x8000 filter bit, then refreshes the list.
evidence: Every row is an item id resolved through Item_LookupRecord, and the three-predicate gate is the 'is this item equippable' test used by the equipment list windows (its siblings filter by kind, equip category and handedness). 'ForMonsters' had no support - no monster record or monster table is read anywhere in the body.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_BuildRowsByEquipCategory
summary: Walks item ids 0..0x24D, keeps equipment ids (0xA4..0x9BF / 0xB19..0xB1C) whose equip-category byte (+0x29) equals the requested style, and appends them to the row table with the filter bit.
evidence: The two tests are literal: the FACTS equipment ranges and then record->f_29 == style, where +0x29 is the documented equip category (the 1H/2H category). 'ByStyle' was vague; 'ByEquipCategory' states the field actually compared.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_BuildRowsByHandedness
summary: Walks item ids 0..0x24D and keeps the weapons accepted by the one-handed (func_0066C5A8) or two-handed (func_0066C5CC) equip-category predicates, appending them to the row table with the filter bit.
evidence: FACTS records 0x0066C5A8 as the 1H check (equip category 0..4) and 0x0066C5CC as the 2H check (5..9), and the body ORs exactly those two calls. Nothing in the function touches kana or name strings, so 'ByKana' was wrong.

name: Ui_ShopWindow_BuildSelectedItemText
signature: void Ui_ShopWindow_BuildSelectedItemText(ShopWindow* self, u32 arg2, int* record)
summary: Builds the shop's selected-item info line (style 0x21): reads the item id from the record's variable-length blob, looks the item up, tests the bag at GameWork+0x24A98 and writes either the owned-count message argument or the item description into the line buffer.
evidence: The bag pointer and Item_LookupRecord are explicit, the message-argument builder is the named Text_FormatMessageArg, and the style id 0x21 is stored first. It only resolves the item row to display its description/count - the item-lookup flag does not apply because the function does not mutate the bag or inventory.

name: Effect_ParticleEmitter_InitPoolA
summary: Creates an effect-emitter part object: runs the scene-node base init for the caller's resource name, allocates a 0xAC-byte emitter (vtable 0x0075AF90), stores the owner at +0x20 and constructs 64 two-word state-sequence entries (ctor 0x006CE2B8); the failure path fills the default colour/fade block from table 0x00725E4C (f_50..f_7C).
evidence: The whole 0x00449A84..0x0044F7xx region is Effect_*Emitter_Setup code (Effect_SphereEmitter_Setup, Effect_Emitter_SetupFromDescriptor, Effect_HelixEmitter_Setup), and the identical D sibling 0x0044EC8C already carries the ParticleEmitter_InitPoolD name; the element ctor 0x006CE2B8 installs std_StateSequence25 per the merged N_123 findings.

name: Effect_ParticleEmitter_InitPoolB
summary: Variant of 0x00449930 with a 0x6C-byte child object (vtable 0x0075AFB4) and 64 single-word entries (ctor 0x006CE608); the default block comes from 0x00725E4C f_30..f_44.
evidence: Same allocate-child template as 0x00449930 in the Effect_*Emitter_Setup region; the element ctor 0x006CE608 is std_StateSequence26 per N_123, and the only differences from A are the object size, vtable and element stride, exactly as the name states.

name: Effect_ParticleEmitter_InitPoolC
summary: Variant of the emitter-pool factory: 0xAC-byte object (vtable 0x0075AFD8), 64 two-word entries (ctor 0x006CE940), defaults from the 14-word table 0x00726114 and an extra scalar f_138 = 0.35.

summary: Child-object factory of a field scene-node class: clears f_2CA, tells the node to apply mode 4 (vtable +0x54), allocates a 0xAC-byte child (vtable 0x0075B0B0), stores the owner at +0x20 and constructs two 0x40-byte state-sequence entries (ctor 0x006CFC98); on failure it clears self[0x13] and copies the default block from 0x00726074.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipPanel_SyncEquipmentChanges
summary: Per-frame equipment-panel poll: when the member index is valid and the current 12-byte equipment snapshot differs from the cached copy, it feeds the changed slot ids to the compare pane (window+0x88 slot +8), recomputes the dual-equip category, applies the accessory effects and stores the new snapshot; otherwise it only decrements the refresh delay f_1C.
evidence: The snapshot compare (func_001009DC(self+2, &self->f_E, 0xC)), the two changed ids passed to window+0x88's slot +8, Item_ClassifyDualEquipCategory and Model_Equip_ApplyAccessoryEffects are all explicit. No arrow or bitmap writes exist, so 'UpdateCompareArrows' invented the arrows; the comparison/apply role is what the body shows.

name: maybe_Ui_TextLine_Reset
summary: Resets one text-line record: id byte 0xFF, float animation/alpha 0.0f, state bytes 0/1, u16 at +0x0A = 0, then clears the 7-wchar text buffer at +0x10 to an empty wide string. The readable C is truncated only because Ghidra mis-marks the wcslen blx 0x00100B74 as noreturn.
evidence: Both named callers are text-layout code (Text_LayoutLines and Ui_Pager_InitTextLayers), which reset their per-line records before filling them, and the twin 0x003D2EE4 has the identical reset prefix and is also called from Text_LayoutLines. No character-status or HP field is read, so 'CharStatusTag' (which came from the wide name buffer) was the wrong reading.
